title: Outlook: Cloud Policy controls for Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows
summary: Hold: the All Accounts example omits the requirement to enable the policy itself before its default and user-override settings take effect. The roadmap facts and surrounding Cloud Policy guidance are supported; the navigation paths need minor completion, and the audit checklist has no corresponding control row.

claims.quote: We’re introducing Cloud Policy service support for Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: The planned controls let admins set default values for supported Outlook settings.
claims.quote: Admins can set default values for supported Outlook settings

claims.claim: Cloud Policy can enforce Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise policy settings on devices that are not domain joined or otherwise managed.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 lets you enforce policy settings for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a user's device, even if the device isn't domain joined or otherwise managed.

claims.claim: Some Cloud Policy settings can be enforced for Office for the web.
claims.quote: You can also enforce some policy settings for Office for the web and Loop, both for guests who are signed in and for users who access documents anonymously.

claims.claim: Learn says most Outlook Cloud Policy settings apply only to classic Outlook.
claims.quote: All ADMX policies and most policies from Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 (Cloud policies) apply only to classic Outlook.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Most mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows and cannot be enabled separately on just one of those clients.
claims.quote: Most of the mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, so you can't enable them on one client but not the other.

claims.claim: Most features are currently managed through Exchange PowerShell, while Cloud Policy manages selected cross-experience features.
claims.quote: You can manage most features with Exchange PowerShell cmdlets. However, for features that span multiple Microsoft 365 experiences, like Loop and in-product Feedback, as well as settings for Diagnostic Data and Connected Experiences, you should use Cloud Policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Priority determines the winning policy setting when users belong to multiple targeted groups with conflicting settings.
claims.quote: If the user is a member of multiple Microsoft Entra groups with conflicting policy settings, priority is used to determine which policy setting is applied. The highest priority is applied, with "0" being the highest priority that you can assign.

claims.claim: New Outlook app-wide settings such as Theme, Diagnostic Data and Connected Experiences depend on the primary account, initially the first account added.
claims.quote: Several App-wide settings, including Theme, Text Size and Spacing, and Diagnostic Data and Connected Experiences are associated with the first account added in new Outlook. This account is considered as the primary account.

claims.claim: When auditing is enabled, Cloud Policy records configuration, setting and priority changes that can be searched in the Purview audit log.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings, and adjustments to priority order are tracked. You can use the portal or PowerShell to search the audit log for such changes.

claims.quote: Searched: "Cloud Policy" "Outlook" "licensing" "charge"; read the full Cloud Policy overview, particularly Licensing requirements. It names supported subscription plans and restrictions, but no separate charge or meter.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Configure Settings reaches the Cloud Policy settings wizard.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies
claims.fix: Complete the wizard route as 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Choose the scope > specific groups > Configure Settings', retaining the note that this roadmap item's settings are not yet listed. The omitted scope selection is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation was found to configure these planned Cloud Policy defaults.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 policy configurations PowerShell Graph API All Accounts unified inbox; "Cloud Policy" "policy configurations" "Graph" "API". Opened Cloud Policy overview; Graph results concern Cloud PCs or audit schemas, not Cloud Policy configuration writes.

claims.claim: The All Accounts path reaches its named Cloud Policy on Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On Configure Settings, search for Show All Accounts view for users with multiple accounts in Outlook for Windows. Open the policy and set Configuration setting to Enabled.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Configure Settings > Show All Accounts view for users with multiple accounts in Outlook for Windows > Configuration setting'. The current route stops on the right policy but before its activation control. See https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/manage/manage-all-accounts-view.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation was found for the All Accounts Cloud Policy default and user-override controls.
claims.quote: Searched: "All Accounts" "Cloud Policy" "PowerShell"; Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 policy configurations PowerShell Graph API All Accounts unified inbox. Opened Manage All Accounts and Cloud Policy overview; neither documents an operation that writes these settings.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: An existing new Outlook All Accounts Cloud Policy pairs a default view with a choice whether users may change that view.
claims.quote: Use Cloud Policy to choose whether All Accounts is shown by default in new Outlook for Windows and whether users can change that behavior.

claims.claim: The All Accounts example tells administrators to set Configure the unified inbox view and Allow user to override this setting without stating that the policy must first be Enabled.
claims.quote: Open the policy and set Configuration setting to Enabled. This activates the policy; the additional settings below determine the view and whether users can change it.
claims.fix: Replace the note's instruction with 'Set Configuration setting to Enabled first, then set Configure the unified inbox view and Allow user to override this setting.' Keep the existing caveat that the setting is not confirmed as part of this roadmap item. Apply the same replacement in the rendered table. See https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/manage/manage-all-accounts-view.

claims.claim: Learn does not identify the existing All Accounts policy as part of this particular roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook on the web new Outlook Cloud Policy default settings user override 571199 rollout licensing; "All Accounts" "Cloud Policy" "PowerShell". Read Manage All Accounts and the roadmap record. The article describes an existing Windows-only policy without linking it to this item.

claims.claim: Exchange admin center > Roles > Outlook web app policies > policy > Manage Features > User experience > Email signature reaches the signature control.
claims.quote: click on the name of the policy > select Manage Features in the Features section > expand the User experience section > uncheck Email signature
claims.fix: Use 'Roles > Outlook web app policies > policy > Features > Manage Features > User experience > Email signature' in the row and table. The missing Features heading is on the cited page; the Roles entry is independently supported by the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/outlook-on-the-web/create-outlook-web-app-mailbox-policy, so the pre-check's missing word is not a blocker.

claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -SignaturesEnabled $false is the Exchange PowerShell operation for disabling manual signature creation in Outlook on the web.
claims.quote: Exchange PowerShell: Use the SignaturesEnabled parameter with the value $false on the Set-OwaMailboxPolicy cmdlet.

claims.claim: Outlook web mailbox policies are assigned to user mailboxes.
claims.quote: You can assign only one Outlook on the web mailbox policy to each user mailbox.

claims.claim: The roadmap description describes settings control, not new data access.
claims.quote: Admins can set default values for supported Outlook settings and choose whether users can change them, providing consistent cloud-based control across their organization

claims.claim: The roadmap describes administrator-set policies, not autonomous behaviour.
claims.quote: Admins can set default values for supported Outlook settings and choose whether users can change them

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not state precedence between a Cloud Policy and an Exchange mailbox policy for the same Outlook on the web setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cloud Policy" "Outlook on the web" "precedence"; opened Cloud Policy overview and Outlook policy management. The documented precedence is over Group Policy and preferences or locally applied policies, not Exchange mailbox policy conflicts for Outlook on the web.

claims.claim: The Exchange mailbox-policy example governs feature availability rather than setting the planned Cloud Policy defaults.
claims.quote: Admins can use either of the following methods to prevent Outlook on the web users from manually creating email signatures: ... Use the SignaturesEnabled parameter with the value $false on the Set-OwaMailboxPolicy cmdlet.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to search the Microsoft Purview audit log, but the controls table has no audit row.
claims.quote: Search the Microsoft Purview audit log for changes to policy configurations, settings and priority order ... The table contains only Cloud Policy defaults, All Accounts view and Exchange mailbox feature controls.
claims.fix: Remove the audit-log search bullet from 'After rollout' so the checklist agrees with the existing controls table; do not add a control row as part of this correction.
